title: Preliminary U.S. Imports for Consumption of Steel Products (Census, Aug 2026 data) — the metals-input read the morning before durable goods
source: EST: census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes) by the durable-goods-2026-09-25 pulse-check sweep. Its 2026 grid carries the row 'Preliminary U.S. Imports for Consumption of Steel Products | September 24, 2026 | 10:00 AM | August 2026', slot id A202609241000, reference period A202608 — the same reference month as the durable-goods advance the next morning. The same grid establishes the monthly cadence independently: 2026-03-25 (Feb data), 04-23 (Mar), 05-26 (Apr), 06-24 (May), 07-27 (Jun), 08-27 (Jul), then 09-24, 10-27, 11-25, 12-22. Filed `estimate` rather than `confirmed` on one count only, and it is not date doubt — this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep, the same limit durable-goods-2026-09-25 itself recorded before its own initial research promoted it off this identical page. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the durable-goods-2026-09-25 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-08, D-17), and it earns a row on two arguments that are specific rather than generic. (1) IT IS THE DATED PRIMARY ON THE ONE CHANNEL THAT LEDGER FLAGGED AND COULD NOT EVIDENCE. Its leg 9 banked primary-metals inventories at $604.4B total with primary metals +1.5% to $51.9B and UP SEVENTEEN CONSECUTIVE MONTHS - called out verbatim as 'a tariff-era stockpiling signature worth watching but not evidenced here'. This release is the monthly Census primary on the import side of exactly that signature, it covers the SAME August reference month, and it lands 10:00 ET on 09-24, the morning BEFORE the 08:30 orders print - a read-ahead, not a restatement. (2) IT IS THE CALIBRATION CASE FOR HOW ONE AGENCY TREATS ITS OWN INDICATORS UNDER A FUNDING LAPSE, AND IT CORRECTS AN OVERSTATEMENT. The durable-goods ledger generalized its M3 finding as 'Census delayed, never deleted'. The same calendar grid refutes the general form: this series' scheduled releases for the December-2025 reference month (slot A202601271000) and the January-2026 reference month (slot A202602251000) BOTH read 'Suspended', with no rescheduled slot anywhere in the published 2026 grid, and the series resumes only with February-2026 data on 2026-03-25. So under the 2025-26 lapse, M3 was delayed ~27-29 days and this indicator was suspended outright - two different fates inside one agency. Honest limit carried with the finding: the program page census.gov/foreign-trade/statistics/steelimports/index.html returned HTTP 404 on direct fetch 2026-09-08, so whether the suspended months' data later appeared elsewhere was NOT verified; the claim made here is exactly what the publisher's own calendar shows, which is the absence of a make-up slot. That matters forward, not backward: the delay-versus-deletion branch migrated from durable-goods-2026-09-25 (closed by the H.R. 6500 signature on 2026-09-02) to durable-goods-2026-12-23, which sits 12 days past the CR's 2026-12-11 expiry, and this series' 12-22 edition sits one day before it. IMPACT LOW, deliberately: no consensus is published for it, no tracked name is symbol-linked, and it lands 10:00 ET on a session already carrying the 7Y auction, SCOOS and the estimate-dated Trump-Xi summit - it is a component read, not a market event. Proposed as an estimate; estimates widen caution, never trigger action.
